title: Synonyms: the trap choices
description: Twenty synonyms at the real pace of thirty seconds each. Every question carries the kinds of wrong answer the SSAT uses most: a word that sounds like the stem, the stem's opposite, a word that often appears near it, and a meaning the stem has in a different sentence. Read all five choices before choosing. A fast wrong answer costs a quarter point; a blank costs nothing.

questions.explanation: Frugal means careful not to waste money or resources. Thrifty is the match. Wasteful is the exact opposite, and opposites are a favourite trap because they sit in the same area of meaning. Poor is close but wrong: a rich person can be frugal by choice. Fruity is a sound-alike.

Diligent means showing steady, careful effort. Hardworking is the match. Lazy is the opposite. Delicate shares a sound, and clever is an association, since diligent students often do well, but cleverness and effort are different things.

Tedious means dull because it is long or repetitive. Boring is the match. Difficult is the trap: tedious work feels like a struggle, but it is usually easy, just endless. Thrilling is the opposite, and tidy and tiny are sound-alikes.

Reckless means acting without thinking about danger or consequences. Rash is the match. Careful is the opposite. Wrecked is a sound-alike, and brave is an association, since reckless people often take risks that can look brave.

Candid means honest and direct, even when the truth is uncomfortable. Frank is the match. Sugary is a trap from the sound of candy. Secretive is the opposite, and shy points the same way, since candid people speak up.

Immense means extremely large. Huge is the match. Tiny is the opposite. Immediate and intense are sound-alikes, and important is an association, since immense things often matter, but size and importance are different.

To scrutinize is to examine something very closely and carefully. Criticize is the trap: people often scrutinize something in order to find fault, and the words even rhyme, but you can scrutinize a painting you admire. Ignore is the opposite.

Amiable means friendly and pleasant to be around. Friendly is the match. Rude is the opposite. Aimless and able share letters with the stem but not its meaning. Talkative is an association, since friendly people often chat.

An ordeal is a long, difficult or painful experience. Painful experience is the match. Order and command are traps from the first syllable, and agreement comes from the end of the word, deal. Celebration is close to the opposite.

Novel, as an adjective, means new and unlike anything before. Original is the match. Lengthy, fictional and printed all describe a novel, the book, which is the noun. When a familiar word appears as a stem, expect its less familiar meaning.
Prudent means showing care and good judgement about the future. Wise is the match. Foolish is the opposite. Proud and rude are sound-alikes, and shy is unrelated.
Obsolete means no longer in use because something better has replaced it. Outdated is the match. Brand new is the opposite. Obvious and absolute are sound-alikes that share only a few letters.
Meager means too small in amount, barely enough. Scanty is the match. Generous is the opposite, and the trap for a reader moving fast. Eager is a sound-alike that differs by one letter.

Tentative means not definite, done as a trial. Uncertain is the match. Certain and permanent are opposites, and having both uncertain and certain in the list is deliberate. Attentive and tense are sound-alikes.

Resilient means able to recover quickly from difficulty, or to spring back into shape. Quick to recover is the match. Fragile is the opposite. Stubborn is the trap, because both words describe someone who does not give up, but a stubborn person refuses to change, while a resilient one bounces back.

Inevitable means certain to happen, impossible to avoid. Avoidable is the opposite. Invisible and invited are sound-alikes. Unfortunate is an association, since people often call bad news inevitable, but good things can be inevitable too.

Vivid means strikingly bright or clear, as in a vivid colour or a vivid memory. Faded and vague are opposites. Living is a trap from the root, which does mean life, but the word is now about brightness. Violent shares the first letters.

Dormant means temporarily inactive, as a volcano or a seed can be. Inactive is the match. Dead is the near miss: a dormant thing can wake up, a dead one cannot. Active is the opposite, and dormitory shares the root, a place for sleeping.
Boisterous means noisy, energetic and cheerful. Rowdy is the match. Quiet is the opposite. Boastful and boyish are sound-alikes, and strong is a guess from the sound of the word.

Elusive means difficult to find, catch or pin down. Hard to catch is the match. Obvious is close to the opposite. Imaginary is the trap, from the sound of illusion: an elusive animal is perfectly real, just hard to find. Electric and exclusive share letters.
